title: Grateful Dead Live at Musikhalle on 1972-04-29
lineage: Dat -> Pro Tools -> Samplitude Professional v10.02 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel (14 inch 16 track Master Reels @ 15ips) -> Dat (44.1k)

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a high‑energy Hamburg show with smoking Pigpen moments and standout performances of Good Lovin', Big Boss Man, Mr. Charlie and a Dark Star→Sugar Magnolia→Caution sequence.
ai_review.review: The Miller transfer delivers an excellent, almost audiophile‑grade soundboard recording that beats every other source for this April‑29‑1972 Hamburg concert. The band is tight and fiery – Pigpen drives the first set while the second set shines with a smoking Dark Star>Sugar Magnolia>Caution stretch, superb Good Lovin', Big Boss Man and an inspired Greatest Story Ever Told. Minor glitches are noted by a few reviewers but they do not detract from what is overall a high‑energy, tightly‑locked performance.

ai_rating.rationale: All eight reviews are 4–5 stars and praise both the show’s energy and the superior soundboard transfer; only minor, isolated flaws are mentioned.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear mix with superb instrument separation; noted as a major upgrade over other sources. A few reviewers mention tiny flaws or occasional dropouts, but overall the recording is pristine.

poor_songs: Next Time You See Me (slow tempo, not a highlight)
Uncle John's Band (a little lost in the middle)
Dark Star (very loose compared to other versions)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Two long, well‑balanced sets. The first set builds with Pigpen’s high‑octane organ and vocal work, while the second set sustains momentum with a strong opening Greatest Story, tight jams, and a climactic Dark Star>Sugar Magnolia>Caution sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for wailing, perfect tone and leading the improvisational flow.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for powerful bass work and vocal contributions (‘singing his butt off’).
band_member_comments.Bob: Recognized for getting deep into lyrics and strong rhythm‑guitar presence.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is highlighted as an additional lead voice, adding fullness to the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (Mickey) described as solid and the glue that keeps everything tied together.
